newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine's Kuchma sacks agriculture minister.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine's Kuchma sacks agriculture minister.

text.p: Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma has sacked Agriculture Minister Anatoly Khorishko but no replacement has been named yet, a press spokesman for Kuchma said on Monday.
"We are still waiting for an official signed order and the name of the new minister," the spokesman said.

Kuchma had referred to "serious inadequacies" in the ministry's work when he announced the decision at a meeting with his prime minister and other senior government officials late on Friday, the spokesman said.
The decision came just ahead of start of Ukraine's spring sowing season, due to start in March.
Kuchma has referred to a need for big cabinet changes several times this year.
He told a meeting of agricultural authorities last month that the ministry's structure, unchanged since the 1940s, did not match up to the task of developing a modern sector.

Khorishko was appointed last summer after a drought which led to a record low grain crop of 25.4 million tonnes against 36.5 million tonnes in 1995. This compared to crops of up to 50 million tonnes regularly produced in Soviet times.
Kuchma said last month that it was "essential" that Ukraine started producing grain at the rate it did in Soviet days within the next two to three years.
"The grain crop losses cost us about $2.5 billion a year and neither nature nor a lack of cash explains that. The reason is the leadership's mistakes," he said.
"Restoring our position in grain production must become a key task for everyone, from the farmer to the head of government," he added.
